articles.title: Forget T. rex — Meet the 43-Foot Sea Monster That Ruled the Ancient Oceans
articles.summary: Paleontologists have unveiled Tylosaurus rex, a massive marine reptile that terrorized seas 80 million years ago. With serrated teeth and a bus-sized body, it's a new species. A fossil called 'The Black Knight' shows a healed broken jaw, proving its resilience.

articles.title: Mars Unmasked: Rusty Dust, Six-Month Summers, and a Volcano That Dwarfs Everest
articles.summary: Mars is more than a red dot — it's a planet of extremes. With a canyon that swallows the Grand Canyon, a volcano three times Everest's height, and confirmed water flows, it's a world of wonder. But watch out: your toes could roast while your face freezes.

articles.title: Australia: A Continent of Extremes — From Sacred Uluru to the Deadly Taipan
articles.summary: Australia is a land of contrasts: the world's largest rock, Uluru, rises from a red desert, while 36 species of poisonous spiders lurk in the east. It's the only country that's also a continent, and nearly a quarter of its people were born overseas.
